h1:
Where to Stay in Songkhla?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Songkhla hotels across every budget — from Sino-Portuguese houses in the old town and the only resort on Samila Beach to 4-star Hat Yai city hotels, a quiet island resort on Ko Yo and a central dorm from ฿315/night. Covering the main areas: Songkhla Old Town, Samila Beach, Ko Yo and Hat Yai. From roughly ฿315–1,800/night.
heroStats: 🏖️ 4 key areas (Old Town·Samila Beach·Ko Yo·Hat Yai)
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right area in Songkhla matter so much?
introHtml: Songkhla isn't one place but feels like several towns in one province, and each area has a completely different vibe. Songkhla Old Town (the Bo Yang quarter, Nang Ngam and Nakhon Nok roads) is the Sino-Portuguese heart — street art, cafés and old eateries you can walk all day. Samila Beach is the in-town beach with its landmark Golden Mermaid statue, ideal if you want to wake to the sea. Ko Yo is a calm island in the lagoon, famous for lakeside sea-bass restaurants and the Tinsulanonda Bridge. And Hat Yai is the shopping-and-food city that draws Malaysian and Singaporean visitors — Kim Yong Market, Lee Garden and Central Festival are all here. Many people book without checking whether their stay is in old Songkhla or in Hat Yai, then lose time shuttling 30–40 minutes back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Songkhla hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Songkhla has no metro. Hat Yai and old Songkhla town are separate districts, about a 30–40 min drive apart. Hat Yai International Airport (HDY) is on the Hat Yai side, about 20–25 min from the city centre, and there's a central railway station in Hat Yai. Exploring the old town, Samila Beach and Ko Yo is easiest with a car or by hailing a Grab. The areas in this guide: Songkhla Old Town — Sino-Portuguese houses, street art, Nang Ngam Road, walkable · Samila Beach — the in-town beach with the Golden Mermaid · Ko Yo — a calm island in the lagoon, lakeside sea bass · Hat Yai — shopping, Kim Yong Market, Lee Garden, Central, easiest access.

entries.name: Casa de Si Boutique House
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score · heritage house by the lagoon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nakhon Nok Rd · Songkhla Old Town, by the lagoon
tags: 🌊 Some rooms with lagoon view + jacuzzi
🗺️ Walk to street art and the City Pillar Shrine
entries.addr: 83 Nakhon Nok Rd, Bo Yang, Mueang Songkhla, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.3 — Casa de Si is a restored Sino-Portuguese house in the heart of Songkhla Old Town, near the lagoon, with vintage-styled rooms that are all different, some with a jacuzzi and lagoon view. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the attentive staff and a location within a few minutes' walk of the street art, the City Pillar Shrine and old cafés, but honestly there aren't many reviews yet (19) as it's a small place, and the stairs up to the upper floors are fairly steep. Best for couples and culture lovers who want to stay in a heritage house right in the old town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a lagoon view, ask for an upper-floor Seaview room when you book. Travelling with elderly guests or heavy luggage? Request a ground-floor room, as the stairs are steep.
pros: Highest score in the guide 9.3 — consistent on Booking and Agoda
Vintage-styled Sino-Portuguese house full of character
Some rooms have a jacuzzi and a Songkhla lagoon view
Walk to street art, the City Pillar Shrine and old cafés
cons: Not many reviews yet (19) as it's a small place
Stairs up to the upper floors are fairly steep and narrow

entries.name: Centara Hotel Hat Yai
entries.badge: 💬 Most reviews 3,300+ · linked to Central mall
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sanehanusorn Rd · heart of Hat Yai
entries.storyHtml: Centara Hotel Hat Yai has the most reviews in this guide — over 3,374 — and Tripadvisor ranks it #1 of 108 Hat Yai hotels. The big draw is a location linked directly to Central Festival Hat Yai: take the lift straight into the mall, and walk to Kim Yong Market and Lee Garden in minutes. Real guest reviews praise the warm service and the location, but note the hotel is showing its age, with dated décor in places and a fairly small pool. Best for those coming to Hat Yai to shop and eat.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a higher floor for city views and less street noise. Shopping? Use the link into Central mall rather than the street — cooler and easier. Book a Free Cancellation rate, as the cancellation policy on cheaper rooms is fairly strict.
pros: Most reviews in the guide 3,374 · Tripadvisor #1 in Hat Yai
Linked directly to Central mall — lift straight in
Warm service guests return for; walk to Kim Yong Market
Has a pool, gym and spa on site
cons: Showing its age, with dated décor and carpets in places
Pool and sauna are fairly small, not resort-style

entries.name: Laguna Grand Hotel & Spa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phawong · between Songkhla and Hat Yai
entries.storyHtml: Laguna Grand is a spa hotel that opened in 2021 with big new rooms, scoring 9.1 from over 508 reviews. The draw is that even entry-level rooms are 35 sqm, plus an outdoor saltwater pool guests love to photograph and an on-site spa, gym and sauna. Real guest reviews praise the newness, the space and the quiet, but it's honest to say the location in Phawong is outside the city, so you'll need a car or a Grab. Best for self-drivers who plan to spend most of their time at the hotel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a pool-view or a Grand Deluxe (42 sqm) for more space and a better view. Phawong is out of town, so plan your transport ahead — you can't walk to malls or markets.
pros: Big new rooms from 35 sqm · score 9.1 from 508 reviews
Lovely saltwater pool with a separate kids' pool
On-site spa, gym and sauna — plenty to do
Large free parking — good for self-drivers
cons: Phawong location is out of town; you need a car or Grab
Some finishes still don't quite feel full five-star

entries.name: Shi-ro-i Poshtel
entries.badge: 🪙 Dorm from ฿360 · top score for budget
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Supasarnrangsan Rd · heart of Hat Yai
tags: 🛏️ Pod beds with curtains and partitions
✨ So clean reviews mention it repeatedly
🚶 Walk to Kim Yong Market and street food
entries.storyHtml: Shi-ro-i Poshtel is a Japanese-style poshtel that scores 9.2 from 336 reviews and a Travelers' Choice award, yet dorm beds start at just ฿360. The draw is pod beds in the dorm with partitions on both sides and a curtain door, so you sleep with the privacy of your own little room, plus the cleanliness that reviews mention most. There are dorm beds and private rooms, and you can walk to Kim Yong Market and city street food. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness and staff, but note the lift and parking are limited. Best for budget travellers and solo travellers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a pair or family? A private room works out better value and more comfortable than booking several dorm beds. Sleeping in the dorm and worried about noise? Pack earplugs, as it's central. Driving? Check on parking first.
pros: Score 9.2 — top among budget stays · 336 reviews · Travelers' Choice
Pod beds with curtains and partitions for privacy
So clean reviews mention it; friendly staff
Private and family rooms · walk to markets and street food
cons: A small place, with limited lift and parking
Dorm uses shared bathrooms; some street noise at times

entries.name: Crystal Hotel Hat Yai
entries.badge: 🏊 Rooftop infinity pool · new design rooms
tags: 🎳 Bowling and a bar in the building
entries.addr: 4 Kanjanavanit Rd Soi 23, Hat Yai, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: Crystal Hotel Hat Yai is a new design hotel with a rooftop infinity pool, scoring 8.9 from 555 reviews. The draw is contemporary minimalist rooms with a clean look, plus a rooftop pool reviewers love to photograph, especially in the evening, with a gym, bowling and a bar in the building. It's near Central Festival, so you can walk to shops and food. Real guest reviews praise the newness, the pool and the value, but note room upkeep isn't consistent across every room, with some aircon or musty-smell issues, and the pool is sometimes closed for events. Best for those wanting a fresh design room near the mall.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Skyline or higher-floor room for city views and more space. If you're set on swimming, check with the hotel whether the pool is closed for an event on your dates.
pros: Rooftop infinity pool with city views
New, clean design rooms · score 8.9 from 555 reviews
Bowling, karaoke and a bar in the building
Near Central Festival — walk to shops and food
cons: Room upkeep inconsistent; some aircon or musty-smell issues
Pool is sometimes closed for weddings or events

entries.name: Buri Sriphu Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sripoovanart Rd · heart of Hat Yai
entries.storyHtml: Buri Sriphu is a 4-star city hotel in central Hat Yai known for value and big parking, scoring 8.9 from 420 reviews. The draw is a central location on Sripoovanart Road, walkable to Greenway Night Market and Central Festival, with a saltwater pool, gym and a large car park with EV chargers that self-drivers love. Real guest reviews praise the clean, spacious rooms and the value, but note it often hosts conferences, so the lobby can be busy when a big group is in. Best for those coming to sightsee, eat and shop, and who drive themselves.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: When a seminar group is in, ask for a higher floor or a room away from the lift for quiet. On long weekends, go down for breakfast early for fuller spread and a calmer room.
pros: Central location, walk to Greenway Night Market and Central
Big car park with EV chargers — rare in central Hat Yai
Clean, spacious rooms with soft beds — good value
Saltwater pool and gym, complete for a central 4-star
cons: Hosts conferences; the lobby can be busy with big groups
Breakfast options thin out when it's full

entries.name: BP Samila Beach Hotel & Resort
tags: 🏖️ On Samila Beach, walk to the sand
🌊 Sea-view rooms, every room with a balcony
entries.addr: 8 Ratchadamnoen Rd, Bo Yang, Mueang Songkhla, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: BP Samila is one of the very few hotels right on Samila Beach — open the curtains in a sea-view room and the bay and the Golden Mermaid are right there, scoring 8.7 from 41 reviews. The draw is the beachfront location, a few steps to the sand, with a private balcony in every room, two pools and breakfast with halal options. Real guest reviews praise the view and location, but it's honest to say it's an older hotel that opened in the late 1990s, with some dated rooms and inconsistent service. Best for those who want to wake to the sea on Samila Beach at an affordable price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pay a little more for a sea-facing Sea View room and ask for a renovated one — that's the whole point of staying here. Step onto the balcony at dawn for sunrise over Samila Bay, the prettiest part of the day.
pros: The only beachfront hotel in Songkhla, walk to the sand
Sea-view rooms open to Samila Bay; every room has a balcony
Two pools and free parking
Varied breakfast with halal and southern Thai options
cons: An older hotel; some rooms dated, paint peeling in places
Service can be unenthusiastic, with a language barrier

entries.name: Baan Nai Nakhon Boutique Hotel
entries.badge: 🏠 Century-old house · owner is your guide
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nang Ngam Rd · Songkhla Old Town
tags: 🚶 Walk to street art and old eateries
entries.addr: 166 Nang Ngam Rd, Bo Yang, Mueang Songkhla, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: Baan Nai Nakhon is a century-old Sino-Portuguese house turned 6-room boutique hotel in the heart of Songkhla Old Town, scoring 8.6 and 4.8/5 on TripAdvisor, ranked #3 of 30 Songkhla hotels. The draw is a roti-and-curry breakfast served in the courtyard garden and an owner who speaks fluent English and knows the old town deeply — like having a private guide. Real guest reviews praise the atmosphere and location, but it's honest to say it's an old wooden house: sound from other rooms carries through the walls, and with only 6 rooms it fills fast. Best for couples and culture lovers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask the owner about old-town walking routes at check-in — that's the real value here. Have breakfast in the garden while the light is still soft for the best atmosphere. If you're a light sleeper, pack earplugs.
pros: Century-old Sino-Portuguese house · TripAdvisor 4.8/5, #3
Roti-and-curry breakfast in the garden, praised in almost every review
Owner speaks fluent English, knows the old town like a guide
Old-town location, walk to street art and old eateries
cons: An old wooden house; sound from other rooms and the street carries
Only 6 rooms, so it fills fast on holidays

entries.name: Sri Koh You Resort
entries.badge: 🌳 Quiet, on an island in the lagoon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ko Yo · on the Songkhla lagoon
tags: 🐟 A base for lakeside sea bass
entries.addr: 57 Moo 4, Ko Yo, Mueang Songkhla, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: Sri Koh You Resort is a small 10-room resort on Ko Yo, an island in the Songkhla lagoon, chosen for its quiet and nature, scoring 8.4 from 12 reviews. The draw is a shady island setting with soft beds, near the Tinsulanonda Bridge, Wat Laem Pho and the lakeside sea-bass restaurants Ko Yo is known for. Real guest reviews praise the quiet and location, but it's honest to say reviews are still few (12), it's a small resort with no pool or on-site restaurant, and nearly all sightseeing needs your own car. Best for self-drivers who want a slow Songkhla trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ko Yo has little public transport, so driving yourself is easiest, with free parking at your door. Check whether breakfast is included when you book; if not, head out to the lakeside sea-bass places around the island.
pros: Quiet and shady, on an island in the Songkhla lagoon
Comfortable rooms, soft beds, restful — and affordable
Near the Tinsulanonda Bridge, Wat Laem Pho and sea-bass spots
Free parking at your door — good for self-drivers
cons: Few reviews still (12); a small resort
No pool or on-site restaurant; you need your own car

entries.name: The Bedrooms Boutique Hotel Hatyai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suwannawong Rd · quiet area, Hat Yai
entries.storyHtml: The Bedrooms is a boutique hotel with big, high-ceilinged rooms in an area quieter than the market centre, from just ฿650, scoring 8.0 from 53 reviews. The draw is rooms that are larger and taller than others at the price, with big bathrooms and free parking, in a quiet area still walkable to Kim Yong Market and Lee Garden. Real guest reviews praise the room size and value, but it's honest to say it's a boutique building starting to show its age, with some musty rooms and imperfect soundproofing. Best for budget travellers who drive themselves.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some rooms have windows facing the corridor; ask for one with an external window for more light and air. The loft rooms have steep stairs with no rail, so if you're with elderly guests or small children, choose a single-level room.
pros: Big high-ceiling rooms with bathrooms larger than expected for the price
Quiet area — restful at night
Free parking and a gym — good for self-drivers
Walk to Kim Yong Market and Lee Garden
cons: A boutique building showing its age; some musty rooms
Soundproofing between rooms isn't great

entries.name: BP Grand Tower Hotel
entries.badge: 💰 Spacious value rooms, walk to Lee Garden
tags: 🚉 Near Kim Yong Market and the station
entries.storyHtml: BP Grand Tower is an older high-rise in central Hat Yai known for location and spacious value rooms, from just ฿850, scoring 7.8 from 200 reviews. The draw is a 5-minute walk to Lee Garden Plaza, near Kim Yong Market and the railway station, with rooms larger than others at a similar price, plus a pool and free parking. Real guest reviews praise the location and value, but it's honest to say it's an old high-rise with inconsistent room condition, some damp and musty rooms, and Wi-Fi that can be unstable. Best for those who put location and value before newness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a high-floor, renovated room at booking or check-in for better condition and a nicer city view. The area is full of dim sum and morning congee shops, so book without breakfast and eat out — cheaper and tastier.
pros: Central location, 5-min walk to Lee Garden
Rooms larger than others at a similar price nearby
Has a pool and free parking
Near Kim Yong Market and the railway station — good value
cons: An old high-rise; some rooms damp and musty
In-room Wi-Fi can be unstable; room condition inconsistent

entries.name: WE Hostel Hatyai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Niphat Uthit area · heart of Hat Yai
tags: 🪙 Dorm bed from ฿315 — cheapest in the guide
🚉 Walk to the station and Lee Garden
entries.addr: Niphat Uthit 2 Rd, Niphat Uthit area, Hat Yai, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: WE Hostel Hatyai is the cheapest stay in this guide, with dorm beds from just ฿315, yet right in central Hat Yai, scoring 7.7 from 128 reviews. The draw is a Niphat Uthit location walkable to Lee Garden Plaza, Kim Yong Market and the railway station, with dorm beds that have privacy curtains, plugs and reading lights. Real guest reviews praise the location and friendly staff, but it's honest to say some beds are old with sagging springs, and being on a central street there's some noise at night. Best for backpackers and solo travellers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want a quiet night? Ask for a bed or room away from the street and pack earplugs. Arriving by train, you can walk your luggage over, as the station is walkable. Staying several nights with the budget? A private room is far more comfortable than the dorm.
pros: Cheapest in the guide, dorm beds from ฿315, central
Dorm beds with privacy curtains, plugs and reading lights
Walk to Lee Garden, Kim Yong Market and the station
Friendly staff who give good travel tips
cons: Some beds are old with sagging springs
On a central street, so noisy at night; shared bathrooms by floor

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Songkhla hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Songkhla?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. Songkhla Old Town suits those who want to walk the Sino-Portuguese houses, street art and cafés (Casa de Si, Baan Nai Nakhon). Samila Beach suits those who want to wake to the sea (BP Samila Beach). Ko Yo suits a quiet stay close to nature (Sri Koh You). Hat Yai suits shopping and eating — Kim Yong Market, Lee Garden, Central (Centara, Buri Sriphu, Crystal, BP Grand Tower, Shi-ro-i, WE Hostel, The Bedrooms). Hat Yai and old Songkhla town are about a 30–40 min drive apart.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Songkhla hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorm beds and hostels start around ฿315–700 per night; boutiques and mid-range to 4-star hotels run ฿1,200–1,800; a small resort on Ko Yo starts around ฿750. All are approximate starting rates for standard rooms. On long weekends and festivals, when Malaysian and Singaporean visitors flock to Hat Yai, prices can be much higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ How are Hat Yai and old Songkhla town different — where should I stay?
faq.a: Hat Yai is the shopping-and-food city — Kim Yong Market, Lee Garden, Central Festival — with the airport and railway station, ideal as a travel base. Old Songkhla town has the Sino-Portuguese old quarter, Samila Beach and Ko Yo, ideal for culture and the sea. They're about 30–40 min apart by road. To see both sides, split your stay between them, or pick Laguna Grand in Phawong, which sits in the middle.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Songkhla hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, 2–3 weeks ahead is enough. But on long weekends, festivals and when Malaysian and Singaporean visitors flock to Hat Yai, good rooms fill very fast, so book a month or more ahead, especially small old-town hotels and beach hotels. Pick a Free Cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Songkhla hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion and period, so it's best to compare all three before booking. Each review page in this guide has price-comparison links — that can save several hundred baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ Is it easy to get around Songkhla without a car?
faq.a: Hat Yai is walkable around its markets and shopping, with a central railway station, but exploring old Songkhla town, Samila Beach and Ko Yo is easiest with a car or a Grab, since they're on the other side from Hat Yai and public transport is limited. Without a car, stay in old Songkhla town (walkable) or central Hat Yai and use Grab now and then.
